headline: Kenny Chesney Returns to Number One for the First Time Since 2019 with ‘Silver Sands Marina’; Kayla Rae Debuts at Number One
body: After nearly seven years, [[Kenny Chesney]] is back on top of the Hot 20. ‘Silver Sands Marina’ rises 2-1 in its 14th week, after three straight weeks as the runner-up, and becomes his 13th #1 single, his first since ‘Tip of My Tongue’ led the chart for one week in November 2019. Only Carrie Underwood (21) and Carly Pearce (18) have more #1s on the chart. To put the wait in perspective, Chesney was a near-constant presence at the top in the chart’s early years. Ten of his first 15 entries went to #1 between ‘The Boys of Fall’ in 2010 and ‘Wild Child’ in 2015, including ‘You and Tequila,’ which spent nine weeks on top in 2011 and still shares the record for the longest-running leader. ‘Better Boat’ and ‘Tip of My Tongue’ followed in 2019, and then the hits got harder to come by. The title track of his 2020 album ‘Here and Now’ stalled at #10, and its follow-up single ‘Happy Does’ never charted at all. ‘Knowing You’ got as close as #4 in 2021, his duet with Kelsea Ballerini, ‘Half of My Hometown,’ peaked at #11, and ‘Everyone She Knows’ reached #9 in 2022. The ‘Born’ era started slowly too, with ‘Take Her Home’ peaking at #16 before ‘Just to Say We Did’ climbed to #4 last year. In all, Chesney put six songs on the chart between #1s, and none got higher than #4. Underneath Chesney is [[Mackenzie Carpenter]], who earns the Greatest Gainer trophy as ‘Kinda Want Your Man’ jumps 5-2, a new peak and her fourth straight Top 5 hit. [[Ella Langley]]’s three-week leader ‘Bottom of Your Boots’ falls 1-3, while [[Ingrid Andress]]’ ‘Tattoos’ slips 3-4 and [[Emily Ann Roberts]]’ ‘Laundry’ moves down one rung, 4-5. [[The Castellows]] hold at #6 with ‘Love Is A Game,’ and [[Wyatt Flores]] stays at #7 with ‘Hate Myself.’ Three songs reach new highs in the bottom half of the Top 10. [[Carly Pearce]] rises 9-8 with ‘She Don’t,’ [[Megan Moroney]] climbs 10-9 with ‘Medicine,’ and rounding out the Top 10 is [[Riley Green]], who moves 11-10 with ‘Imagine That.’ It is his first Top 10 hit on his own. Interestingly, all four of Green’s Hot 20 entries have now reached the Top 10, and the first three were duets: ‘You Look Like You Love Me’ with Langley went to #1 in January 2025, their follow-up ‘Don’t Mind If I Do’ peaked at #3, and ‘If I Don’t Leave I’m Gonna Stay’ with Pearce reached #10 this spring. Making room, [[Kip Moore]]’s ‘Faith in the Wind’ falls 8-11. [[Flatland Cavalry]] rise 13-12 with ‘Never Coming Back’ and [[Kacey Musgraves]] moves 14-13 with ‘Mexico Honey,’ both new peaks, while [[Ashley Cooke]]’s ‘High School Sweetheart’ slips 12-14. Langley’s ‘Broken’ climbs 17-15, and Musgraves’ ‘Loneliest Girl’ and [[Alana Springsteen]]’s ‘Love Me Anyway’ each slide down one rung, 15-16 and 16-17. [[Maddie Font]] (‘Drive Me Around’), [[Carter Faith]] (‘If I Had Never Lost My Mind’) and [[Miranda Lambert]] (‘Two Things Can Be True’) hold at #18, #19 and #20. With no debuts and no songs falling off, it is the same 20 songs as last week. Musgraves also picks up a Platinum certification this week for her album ‘Middle of Nowhere.’

On the Pop 10, [[Kayla Rae]] makes a splash as ‘It Wasn’t Nothing’ debuts at #1, her fourth #1 single after ‘Someone New,’ ‘Wasted’ and ‘Blue.’ It is her 16th Pop 10 entry and the first time she has debuted at #1; her previous best debut was ‘True,’ which entered at #2 last December. It is also the 31st song to debut at #1 on the Pop 10, and the fourth this year. [[Cassandra Coleman]]’s three-week leader ‘End of Your Love’ falls 1-2, and [[Roxy Dekker]] slips 2-3 with ‘Ver Van M’n Bed.’ The Greatest Gainer is [[Peach PRC]], whose ‘Eucalyptus’ climbs 5-4 to a new peak. [[Aitana]]’s ‘6 of Febrero’ falls 3-5 and [[Karol G]]’s ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ slips 4-6. [[Adela]] (‘Nicole Kidman’) and [[Taylor Swift]] (‘Patient Zero’) each move down one rung, 6-7 and 7-8. [[Ashe]] holds at #9 with ‘Stop the Wedding,’ and rounding out the Top 10 is [[Olivia Rodrigo]] and [[Chappell Roan]]’s ‘Expectations,’ which stays at #10. Making room for Kayla Rae, [[Ellie Goulding]]’s ‘Black Prada Dress’ falls off the chart from #8 after peaking at #4.

headline: ‘Bottom of Your Boots’ Still Number One; Moroney Enters Top 10, Langley Debuts ‘Broken’
body: [[Ella Langley]] holds the top spot on the Hot 20 for a third week with ‘Bottom of Your Boots,’ her seventh #1 single. She also earns the week’s Hot Shot Debut, as ‘Broken’ enters at #17, giving her two songs on the chart. Underneath Langley, [[Kenny Chesney]] holds the #2 position for a third straight week with ‘Silver Sands Marina,’ and [[Ingrid Andress]] stays at #3 with ‘Tattoos.’ Behind them, three singles reach new peaks. [[Emily Ann Roberts]] rises 5-4 with ‘Laundry,’ [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] climbs 6-5 with ‘Kinda Want Your Man,’ and [[The Castellows]] move 7-6 with ‘Love Is A Game.’ In fact, Carpenter has now taken all four of her Hot 20 entries into the Top 5. [[Wyatt Flores]] climbs 8-7 with ‘Hate Myself,’ another new high. [[Kip Moore]]’s ‘Faith in the Wind’ slips 4-8, one week after reaching its peak, while [[Carly Pearce]] rises 10-9 with ‘She Don’t.’ Rounding out the Top 10 is [[Megan Moroney]], who moves 11-10 with ‘Medicine.’ Remarkably, all nine of her Hot 20 entries have now reached the Top 10. Just outside, [[Riley Green]] rises 12-11 with ‘Imagine That,’ and [[Ashley Cooke]] earns the Greatest Gainer trophy, jumping 17-12 with ‘High School Sweetheart.’ [[Flatland Cavalry]] also gain five spots, rising 18-13 with ‘Never Coming Back.’ Kacey Musgraves’ ‘Mexico Honey’ slips 13-14, and her four-week leader ‘Loneliest Girl’ falls 9-15. [[Alana Springsteen]] holds at #16 with ‘Love Me Anyway,’ while [[Maddie Font]] (‘Drive Me Around’) and [[Carter Faith]] (‘If I Had Never Lost My Mind’) each move down one rung, 19-18 and 20-19. Closing out the chart is [[Miranda Lambert]], whose ‘Two Things Can Be True’ debuts at #20. It is her 34th Hot 20 entry, one shy of Carrie Underwood’s record. Making room, Mackenzie Carpenter’s ‘All In Already’ and Flatland Cavalry and Kaitlin Butts’ ‘A Life Where We Work Out’ fall off the chart.

On the Pop 10, [[Cassandra Coleman]] spends a third week at #1 with ‘End of Your Love.’ [[Roxy Dekker]] holds at #2 with ‘Ver Van M’n Bed,’ while [[Aitana]] climbs 4-3 with ‘6 of Febrero,’ a new peak and her fourth Top 5 hit, though she is still looking for her first #1. [[Karol G]]’s 1-week leader ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ slips 3-4. The Greatest Gainer is [[Peach PRC]], whose ‘Eucalyptus’ jumps 8-5 to a new high, and [[Adela]] also gains three spots, rising 9-6 with ‘Nicole Kidman.’ [[Taylor Swift]]’s ‘Patient Zero’ falls 5-7 and [[Ellie Goulding]]’s ‘Black Prada Dress’ slips 6-8. [[Ashe]] moves 10-9 with ‘Stop the Wedding’ in its second week. The week’s only debut comes from [[Olivia Rodrigo]] and [[Chappell Roan]], whose ‘Expectations’ enters at #10. It is Rodrigo’s eighth Pop 10 entry and Roan’s tenth. To make room, girlsweetvoiced’s three-week leader ‘Cranberry’ falls off the chart from #7.

headline: ‘Bottom of Your Boots’ Still Number One; Emily Ann Roberts Enters Top 5
body: [[Ella Langley]] remains atop the Hot 20 for a second week with ‘Bottom of Your Boots.’ The single is Langley’s seventh #1, and remarkably, every one of her 11 entries on the chart has reached the Top 5. Underneath Langley is [[Kenny Chesney]], who holds the #2 position for a second week with ‘Silver Sands Marina.’ It is his highest charting single since 2019’s ‘Tip of My Tongue.’ The big mover this week is Kacey Musgraves’ four-week leader ‘Loneliest Girl,’ which falls 3-9. Because of this, the next six singles each climb one rung. [[Ingrid Andress]] rises 4-3 with ‘Tattoos,’ a new peak in its 15th week, while [[Kip Moore]] moves 5-4 with ‘Faith in the Wind,’ which reaches a new high in its 22nd week on the chart. New to the Top 5 is [[Emily Ann Roberts]], who rises 6-5 with ‘Laundry,’ her first career Top 5. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] climbs 7-6 with ‘Kinda Want Your Man,’ [[The Castellows]] move 8-7 with ‘Love Is A Game’ and [[Wyatt Flores]] rises 9-8 with ‘Hate Myself,’ his first Top 10. [[Carly Pearce]] holds at #10 with ‘She Don’t.’ Just outside the Top 10, [[Riley Green]] earns the week’s Greatest Gainer trophy, jumping 14-12 with ‘Imagine That,’ while [[Kacey Musgraves]] rises 15-13 with ‘Mexico Honey,’ giving her two songs in the Top 13. There are no debuts this week, with #16 through #20 holding in place.

On the Pop 10, [[Cassandra Coleman]] holds #1 for a second week with ‘End of Your Love,’ her fifth #1 single. In fact, the entire Top 7 stays put this week, the first time that has happened in at least a year. [[Roxy Dekker]] remains at #2 with her 1-week leader ‘Ver Van M’n Bed,’ ahead of [[Karol G]]’s 1-week leader ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ at #3 and [[Aitana]]’s ‘6 of Febrero’ at #4, meaning three of the Top 4 are sung in a language other than English. [[Taylor Swift]] holds #5 with ‘Patient Zero.’ Interestingly, Swift has now placed eight songs on the Pop 10 but is still seeking her first #1. [[Ellie Goulding]] stays at #6 with ‘Black Prada Dress’ and [[girlsweetvoiced]] holds #7 with the three-week leader ‘Cranberry.’ Below them, [[Peach PRC]] rises 9-8 with ‘Eucalyptus’ and [[Adela]] climbs 10-9 with ‘Nicole Kidman,’ both new peaks. [[Ashe]] is the week’s only debut, entering at #10 with ‘Stop the Wedding,’ her first appearance since 2021’s #1 ‘Till Forever Falls Apart.’ Coleman’s ‘Midnight Blue’ falls off the chart from #8 to make room.
